To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the H protein of MV contains at least four immunogenic T cell regions, one of which is a dominant epitope in BALB/c mice; (2) T cell recognition of the H protein is influenced by H-2 type, as the dominant epitope is not the same in both mouse strains; and (3) the T cell repertoire is broader following immunization with synthetic peptides than after infection with virus
the helper T cell repertoire for measles virus haemagglutin epitopes is broader in mice following immunization with synthetic peptides than after immunization with live virus.
the H protein contains a number of T cell epitopes which are recognized by lymphocytes primed in vivo with the whole protein and that the T cell epitope repertoire of the H protein is broad.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of T cell epitopes in the H protein of MV and the effect of the mouse H-2 haplotype on T cell epitope recognition.
the identification of the helper T cell antigen sites of MV in mice.
the identification of helper T cell epitope(s) in mice from the MV H protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the H protein of MV has a number of T cell epitopes which are recognized by lymphocytes from both BALB/c and TO mice.
the T cell epitopes in the H protein of MV are not restricted to a single region of the protein and that the epitopes are not easily predicted by the algorithms.
the H protein of MV contains a number of T cell epitopes which differ between mouse strains and that these epitopes can be identified using synthetic peptides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the helper T cell antigen recognition sites of the MV H protein are restricted and differ between mouse strains, and that the prediction of helper T cell epitope sites from sequence data is not yet reliable.
the T cell recognition of the H protein of MV is complex and that the repertoire of T cell epitopes is broader than the repertoire of epitopes recognized following immunization with whole virus.
the helper T cell repertoire for MV-H is broader than previously thought and that the epitopes are strain-specific.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the T cell epitopes identified in mice are not necessarily those predicted to be immunodominant by the various algorithms.
it is important to use experimental data to define helper T cell epitope regions on viral proteins.
the T cell epitopes of the H protein are strain-specific, which is important for the design of vaccines against this virus.
